criteria: Additional combined-season trials passing the non-physical gates and not yet included in the earlier relaxed-cut review. Strongest holdout trial per new target at this checkpoint. This selection uses inspected scores and is exploratory.

targets.review: Not promoted. The filtered fold has multiple broad minima and substantial oscillation outside the selected window; before the periodic model the same window is a broad brightening. Its interpretation depends strongly on filtering.

The difference signal is displaced by about 1.17-1.20 pixels from the intended target in all three observed sectors. Reject this trial as evidence for a planet on the intended nearby star. The approximate sky locations lie toward catalogued neighboring sources; the particular contaminant is not uniquely identified by this simple centroid diagnostic.
targets.limitations: No precision PRF fit or formal astrometric uncertainty. No classification or novelty claim for the contaminating source.

targets.review: Not promoted. The training fold shows a broad baseline trough across most of the displayed interval, without a distinct short transit; the holdout shape differs.
Not promoted. The folded deficit is broad and changes with periodic filtering, with comparable surrounding structure. It does not provide a compelling isolated transit shape.

The 5.29820-day trial is an approximately six-fold alias of a 0.883-day variation. Dimming occurs in every one of the six phase classes, in both training and holdout sectors, rather than only at the selected long-period ephemeris. The fixed P/6 diagnostic gives nominal training S/N 21.2 and holdout S/N 10.1. No additional temperate-planet candidate is promoted.
targets.limitations: Pixel differences are near the target at this resolution, but an approximately four-arcsecond catalogued neighbor remains unresolved. The source and physical cause of the shorter variability are not established. These are post-review diagnostics, and do not rule out other planets.
